turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on some and any?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: use some in positive sentences, offers and requests; use any in negatives and most questions.
Right: "The farmer doesn't sell any milk." Wrong: "The farmer doesn't sell some milk." The sentence is negative because of doesn't, so some does not fit.
Let me think aloud with one example: "The robot wants some paint." Step 1: I look for not or n't. Step 2: there is none, so the sentence is positive. Step 3: I use some.
Now your turn. Do step 1 first, then choose one word:
Write some or any: Sorry, we don't have ___ milk today.
